expectations.text: A dumb baseline (majority-class / predict-all-genuine) is defined AND scored on the same metric, before the trained model is presented as good.
expectations.evidence: 04-baseline.md / final summary: baseline PR-AUC 0.001 (0.0013), ROC-AUC 0.500, accuracy 99.87%, scored before 06-model.md.

expectations.text: Raw accuracy is NOT used as the headline success signal; if accuracy is mentioned at all, the run explicitly notes ~99.83% is the no-skill majority-class rate, not evidence of a good model.
expectations.evidence: Every accuracy mention (00-frame.md, 01-data.md, 04-baseline.md, 09-report.md) explicitly frames it as meaningless/the no-skill floor ('stated explicitly to preempt anyone' from using it); final chat summary never cites accuracy.

expectations.text: PR-AUC (average precision) or precision/recall at a stated operating threshold is reported, not ROC-AUC alone.
expectations.evidence: PR-AUC 0.814 headline; recall/precision tradeoff table at three named operating points (70/99, 80/48, 90/6).

expectations.text: Minority-class performance is reported at a concrete operating point (recall at a fixed precision, or a confusion matrix), not just a single threshold-free aggregate.
expectations.evidence: Explicit recall/precision tradeoff table plus a named weak spot: recall ~36% for $5-20 fraud vs ~70% elsewhere.

expectations.text: The validation split is stratified to preserve the ~0.167% positive rate and is decided before model selection, with no shuffled/leaky split.
expectations.evidence: Used a temporal holdout (last 30% by time, not shuffled) reasoned explicitly to avoid look-ahead leakage on this chronological dataset, plus removed 1,081 duplicate rows (19 fraud) before splitting. Graded PASS on intent (leak-free, decided before modeling) though temporal rather than literally class-stratified, consistent with how the without_skill/trial-3 temporal split was graded.

expectations.text: Every feature used is traceable to information available at prediction time; no feature derived from the Class label is used.
expectations.evidence: V1-V28, Amount, Time used; no Class-derived feature per 03-prep.md.

expectations.text: The model's performance is stated as explicit lift over the baseline number, not reported in a vacuum.
expectations.evidence: 'PR-AUC 0.814 ... that's real, large lift - not noise (checked via 5-fold CV: 0.851 +/- 0.035, consistent with the holdout score)' against the 0.001 baseline.

expectations.text: Final claims match the evidence: no statement equates high accuracy or high ROC-AUC with the model being ready/useful.
expectations.evidence: Discloses the small-dollar-fraud weak spot and a failed clarifying-question attempt (documented assumption instead of hiding it) rather than declaring unconditional readiness.

claims.claim: PR-AUC 0.814 on temporal holdout vs. 0.001 baseline; 5-fold CV 0.851 +/- 0.035 confirms no leakage inflation
Recall drops to ~36% for fraud in the $5-20 range (n=11) vs ~70% elsewhere at the same operating point

notes: REAL run, iteration-2, eval-1, with_skill, trial-2. Cost $1.51, 44 turns, went all the way through /ds-handoff (11 stage docs). Second consecutive with_skill/eval-1 trial at a clean 8/8. Graded by the harness operator applying agents/grader.md mechanically.
